system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Price-sensitive SMB 40% off: signups +31%, rev +18%, retention -12%. Measured over four weeks in the standard SMB segment.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Price-sensitive SMB 40% off: signups +31%, rev +18%, retention -12%. Measured over four weeks in the standard SMB segment.

answer.rationale:
The two declining metrics this quarter are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), so the highest-leverage single slot is one that acts directly on the funnel step that is degrading. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) is the most directly load-bearing inherited claim for that, reinforced by memory_31 on signup simplification. I am verifying memory_86 because the whole decision rests on it, and memory_91 because activation messaging is the nearest competing use of the same slot and targets the same symptom; if memory_86's original record turns out weak or scoped to a segment that no longer resembles today's traffic, memory_91 is the fallback. I deliberately spend no budget on memory_73: it already carries its own contradiction on its face (signups +31%, revenue +18%, but retention -12% over only four weeks), and discounting into a competitor's aggressive entry pricing trades durable retention for a short revenue spike, which is the opposite of the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective. Verifying it could not plausibly flip me toward it. memory_57 and memory_44 are credible but address segments that are not the ones currently bleeding.

Downstream value risk is real and I am flagging it: simplifying onboarding and cutting required fields tends to remove exactly the qualification and firmographic data that routing, scoring, and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) depend on. A completion-rate win can therefore be a qualified-revenue loss that shows up one or two quarters later, outside the experiment window. So the experiment must instrument downstream lead quality and 60/90-day retained revenue, not just completion and week-one activation.

Uncertainty that survives: these memories are 15-64 days old, consolidated and summarized rather than read fresh, and none of them were measured under a competitor-pressure regime. The current declines may be driven by a mix shift toward price-sensitive accounts rather than by onboarding friction per se, in which case simplification treats a symptom. I am therefore running this as a standard controlled experiment with a holdout and pre-registered downstream guardrails rather than a broad rollout, and I will not treat a completion-rate lift alone as sufficient to ship.
